We need to:
Assign the first usable host IP address to R1.
Assign the last usable host IP address to R2.
Verify connectivity using ping.
Assumption: IPv4 Subnet Given (Example: 192.168.1.0/30)
Network Address: 192.168.1.0/30
Subnet Mask: 255.255.255.252
Usable IPs:
First Usable (R1): 192.168.1.1
Last Usable (R2): 192.168.1.2

Broadcast IP: 192.168.1.3
Steps to Configure IPv4
On R1:
bash
Copy
Edit
configure terminal
interface GigabitEthernet0/0
ip address 192.168.1.1 255.255.255.252
no shutdown
exit
write memory
On R2:
bash
Copy
Edit
configure terminal
interface GigabitEthernet0/0
ip address 192.168.1.2 255.255.255.252
no shutdown
exit
write memory
Verify IPv4 Connectivity:
On R1, test ping to R2 (192.168.1.2):
bash
Copy
Edit
ping 192.168.1.2
On R2, test ping to R1 (192.168.1.1):
bash
Copy
Edit

ping 192.168.1.1
If successful, it confirms IPv4 connectivity.

no shutdown
exit

ipv6 address 2001:DB8:ACAD:1::2/64
no shutdown

exit
